questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design precise, namespace-scoped RBAC changes and validate with can-i commands, a common real-world task in security-conscious orgs.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped RBAC
- Roles vs RoleBindings
- can-i validation
- Audit-friendly changes

## Implementation Steps

**1. Create Namespace and ServiceAccount**
```bash
kubectl create namespace tenant-a
kubectl create serviceaccount batch-sa -n tenant-a
```

**2. Apply RBAC Configuration**
```yaml
# Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: read-pods-cm
  namespace: tenant-a
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]

# RoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: batch-sa-read-pods-cm
  namespace: tenant-a
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: read-pods-cm
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: batch-sa
  namespace: tenant-a
```

**3. Verify Access Controls**
```bash
# Test allowed access
kubectl auth can-i get pods --as=system:serviceaccount:tenant-a:batch-sa -n tenant-a
kubectl auth can-i get configmaps --as=system:serviceaccount:tenant-a:batch-sa -n tenant-a

# Test denied Secret access
kubectl auth can-i get secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:tenant-a:batch-sa -n tenant-a
# Expected output: no
```

**4. Sample Job Manifest**
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: test-batch-job
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: batch-sa
      containers:
      - name: test-container
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests hands-on ability to apply Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for multi-namespace isolation and least privilege, including default-deny and per-port allow rules, plus practical troubleshooting steps.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics
- namespaceSelector and podSelector
- Ingress vs Egress rules and reciprocity
- Troubleshooting pod reachability with test pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# api-prod-default-deny
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-default-deny
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```

```yaml
# api-prod-to-logging (allow egress to logging)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-to-logging
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: logging
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

```yaml
# logging-accept-api-prod (allow ingress from api-prod to logging)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: logging-accept-api-prod
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logging
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: api-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

```yaml
# api-prod-to-db (allow egress to db-prod on 5432)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-to-db
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: db-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
```

```yaml
# db-accept-api-prod (allow ingress from api-prod to db)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: db-accept-api-prod
  namespace: db-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: api-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
```

- How would you roll back if a required path is blocked by policy?
